title: Where Does Rain Come From? Science for Kids with Gizmo
description:
Where does rain come from? Find out with Gizmo the robot: the sun warms water and turns some of it into invisible water vapor, cold air high up turns the vapor back into tiny drops that gather on specks of dust and make clouds, and drops that grow too heavy fall as rain. Small raindrops are round and bigger ones are shaped like a hamburger bun.
A science explainer for kids ages 4-8, with questions to answer, things to copy, quick checks and a quiz at the end.

Where the facts come from (read Nov 19, 2026): USGS Water Science School, The Water Cycle for Kids and Are Raindrops Shaped Like Teardrops?; NOAA SciJinks, What Causes Rain?
facts: USGS Water Science School, 'The Water Cycle for Kids', water.usgs.gov/edu/watercycle-kids-beg.html (read Nov 19 2026): 'The sun causes liquid water to evaporate, or turn from a liquid to a gas (water vapor).' 'The invisible water vapor floats high into the atmosphere' 'The colder temperatures high in the atmosphere cause the water vapor to turn back into tiny liquid water droplets' 'Condensation causes clouds to form.' 'When they get heavy enough, they fall to Earth as precipitation, such as rain and snow.' 'When rain hits the land or snow melts, it flows downhill over the landscape.' 'most of it ending up back in the oceans.' 'This process is always happening everywhere.'

NOAA SciJinks, 'What Causes Rain?', scijinks.gov/rain (read Nov 19 2026): 'In order to condense, the water vapor must have a solid to glom onto.' 'This solid "seed" may be a speck of dust or pollen' 'with more water condensing onto other water droplets, the droplets grow.' 'When they get too heavy to stay suspended in the cloud ... they fall to Earth as rain.'

USGS Water Science School, 'Raindrops are Different Shapes' (Are raindrops shaped like teardrops?), usgs.gov/water-science-school/science/are-raindrops-shaped-teardrops (read Nov 19 2026): 'Small raindrops (radius < 1 millimeter (mm)) are spherical; larger ones assume a shape more like that of a hamburger bun.' 'The artistic representation of raindrop as presented by popular culture is that of a teardrop.'
improves: second Gizmo explainer: three new places (beach hello, mountain clouds, river rain) and three moving examples (a puddle that shrinks while vapor rises, a speck of dust a droplet grows on, a cloud that rains)
invisible things are shown and said to be drawn ('we drew it with little dots'), so the picture does not teach that vapor can be seen
the quiz is three answer-sign rounds on the teaching board (no check mark beside a face)

segments.name: hello
lines: Hello, friends! I am Gizmo the robot.
wide
Today we are finding out where rain comes from!
orbit
My little helper bot is here too. Hello, little bot!
dolly
We have three big questions. Count them with me. One, two, three!
Ready? Let's find out!

segments.name: vapor

lines.t: Where does the water for rain come from?
Does it come from the sea? Or from the Moon?

lines: It comes from the sea, and from lakes, and even from puddles!
Here is the fun fact. The sun warms the water, and some of it turns into a gas, called water vapor.
This is called evaporation. Look! The puddle is getting smaller.

lines.t: Can we see water vapor? Hmm.

lines: No! Water vapor is invisible. We drew it with little dots, so you can see where it goes.
Up, up, it floats!
close:host
The water vapor floats high up into the air.
The sun's warmth helps water change, from a liquid, into a gas.
Liquid water is like the water in a puddle. A gas is like the air.
And this is happening everywhere, all the time!
Over the sea, over the lakes, and over the puddles too.
Say it with me. The sun turns water into vapor!
close:host
Can you wiggle your fingers up high, like rising water vapor?
Up, up, up! Now float your hands down, nice and slow.

lines.t: Quick check! Can you see water vapor? Yes? Or no?

lines: No! It is invisible. Great job!

short.title: Can You See Water Vapor? Science for Kids
short.fact: The sun warms water and turns some of it into invisible water vapor, which floats high into the air (USGS, The Water Cycle for Kids).

segments.name: clouds

lines.t: How does a cloud form, high up in the sky?
Does the water vapor get colder? Or warmer?

lines: It gets colder!
Here is the fun fact. High up in the sky, the air is cold.
The cold turns the water vapor back into tiny drops of liquid water.

lines.t: But tiny drops need something to hold on to. What is it? Hmm.

lines: A speck of dust, or a bit of pollen! The water gathers on it.
The water vapor holds on to the speck, and turns into a tiny drop.
The tiny drop grows, and grows!
teach
Lots and lots of tiny drops together make a cloud.
This change, from vapor back into water, is called condensation.
Puff, puff! The cloud floats along, high in the sky.
So a cloud is made of water. Who knew?
Say it with me. Cold air turns vapor into clouds!
close:host
Can you make a cloud shape with your arms? Big and round!
Now float like a cloud. Drift, drift, drift.

lines.t: Quick check! A cloud is made of tiny drops of what? Water? Or sand?

lines: Tiny drops of water! You got it!

short.title: How Does a Cloud Form? Science for Kids
short.fact: Cold air high up turns water vapor back into tiny drops of water, which gather on specks of dust or pollen; condensation makes clouds (USGS, The Water Cycle for Kids; NOAA SciJinks, What Causes Rain?).

segments.name: rain

lines.t: What makes the drops in a cloud fall down as rain?
Do they get too heavy? Or too sleepy?

lines: They get too heavy!
Here is the fun fact. More and more water gathers on the drops, and they grow bigger.
When they get too heavy to float, they fall down as rain. Pitter, patter!
Down, down, down they fall, all the way to the ground.

lines.t: What shape is a falling raindrop? Hmm.

lines: Small raindrops are round, like a ball. Bigger ones look like a hamburger bun!
Not like a teardrop at all!
teach
The rain lands on the ground, and flows downhill.
Down into streams and rivers, and back to the sea.
Then the sun warms the water again, and around and around it goes!
This is called the water cycle. It is always happening, everywhere!
Around and around, again and again!
Say it with me. Heavy drops fall down as rain!
close:host
Can you tap your fingers like falling rain? Pitter, patter!
Faster, faster! Now slow, slow, and stop.

lines.t: Quick check! Is a big raindrop shaped like a teardrop? Or a hamburger bun?

lines: A hamburger bun! Super thinking!

short.title: What Shape Is a Raindrop? Science for Kids
short.fact: Cloud drops grow until they are too heavy and fall as rain; small raindrops are round and bigger ones are shaped like a hamburger bun (NOAA SciJinks; USGS Water Science School).

segments.name: quiz
lines: Wow! We found out so much today. Now it is quiz time!
Get ready. Think hard!

lines.t: Question one. What turns water into water vapor? The sun? Or the wind?

lines: The sun! Yes!

lines.t: Question two. What is a cloud made of? Tiny drops of water? Or cotton?

lines: Tiny drops of water! That's right!

lines.t: Question three. When cloud drops get too heavy, what happens? They fall as rain? Or they fly away?

lines: They fall as rain! You remembered!

segments.name: goodbye
lines: You found out so much today.
wide
The sun lifts water up as vapor. Cold air makes clouds. And heavy drops fall down as rain!
orbit
What would you like to find out next?
dolly
Thank you for exploring with me. Bye-bye, friends! See you next time!
wide
